$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}S_{d}\bigr)=d!^{-1}\prod_{1}^{d}|Y_{i}| , $$

and ${\mathbb P}\{J_{1},\ldots ,J_{d}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
With ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\Bigr)^{d}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $0$–volume being obtained on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.
For $i\ne j$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|
     +\frac{d-1}{d}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}}
   =I+\frac{C}{d}, $$

$${\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|=\frac23,\qquad 
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196,$$

$C=2/3-I\approx-0.098529$.  In particular
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and for the ${d+1\choose2}$ unordered pairs of
$S_{d}$

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
          {\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
   =\frac{(d-1)^{2}S+5d-2}{3d(d+1)},$$

$S=\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with the
${d+1\choose2}$–pair average

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)\!\left[I+C/d\right]}
   =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=(1/16)\times3/\!\left[1+I+C/2\right]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and the tail is $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
   \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and the first non-trivial
correction $R_{2}\approx0.109$.  Up to the usual $d=1$ normalisation
this is the $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E{\rm dist}_{d}$ i.i.d. cross constant,
$1.12$ to two figures.  In particular the $X_{i}-X_{j}$ pair
normalisation $r_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$
gives $r_{1}=1$, $r_{2}\approx0.0873$, $r_{3}\approx0.00632,\dots$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}\approx1.094$, the $1.09$–$1.10$ value quoted for the
point–point normalisation. ∎

1.text:
For the cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$ put 
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$, 
$K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d. and
${\cal S}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}{\cal S}_{d})
   =\dfrac{|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\dfrac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|}{d!}$,
hence with ${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|U|\Bigr)^{d}
     \frac{d!}{d^{d}}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
i.e. ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ on the i.i.d. cross model.

For $i\ne j$

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$, 
${\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

Hence

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =I+\frac{2/3-I}{d}, \qquad 
C:=\frac23-I\approx-0.098529 .
$$

The mean unordered distance of the $d+1$ points of ${\cal S}_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}, \qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

so that with the usual average over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In closed form

$$
R_{d}= \frac{(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
            {\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]/3},
$$

and

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$
* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}\ldots$
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is therefore
essentially the first two terms,

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx 1.117\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$
to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and
$R_{2}\approx0.109$ accounting for $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.
Removing the $d=1$ normalisation the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$ only ratio
$r_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}$ sums to $ \approx1.094$, the familiar
$1.09\!-\!1.12$ cross constant.

*Remark.*  On the usual bijective, one-point-per-axis reading
$K_{i}=i$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, 
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and

$$
R_{d}^{\rm det}= \frac{2^{-d}(d+1)}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

$R_{1}^{\rm det}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm det}\approx0.212$, $R_{3}^{\rm det}
\approx0.033$, etc., the often quoted
$\,\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=e^{1/2}-1$ normalised by $I$. ∎

8.text:
For the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}}$, $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $J_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Put
$|Y|\sim U(0,1)$ and $E|Y|=1/2$,

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}S_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{1}^{d}|Y_{i}|}{d!}{\bf1}_{\{J_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}}, $$

so that with ${\mathbb P}\{J_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$

\begin{equation*}
E V_{d}= \frac{1}{d!}\Bigl(E|Y|\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
       =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E V_{1}=1/2,
\end{equation*}
in particular $E V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.
For $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}E\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}},\qquad 
E|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|=2/3, $$

and with $I_{0}=\displaystyle\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv$

$$I_{0}= \frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196, $$

so that
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)3I_{0}]/3d$.
Writing $S=\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1=3I_{0}$ the mean distance of a
uniformly chosen unordered pair of $S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
       =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
       =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2, $$

and

$$R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)d^{\,1-d}2^{-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},
     \qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e. $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}=3\cdot3\cdot2^{-1}2^{-2}/[8+S]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}=1/6/[13+4S]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

etc.  The series is dominated by the first two terms,

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.1172, $$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, $R_{1}=1$ being the
one–dimensional contribution and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ the first non–trivial
correction.  With the conventional $d\!+\!1$–point average this is the
$EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ volume–to–mean–pairwise–distance constant for the
i.i.d. uniform–on–the–cross model; the pair-only normalisation
$EV_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ is $ \approx1.09\!-\!1.10$.

On the distinct–axes, bijective normalisation $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,
$EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I_{0}]/(d+1)$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I_{0}]$, whence
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation. ∎

9.text:
For the $d$ points write $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.
and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Put
$|Y|\sim U(0,1)$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}S_{d}\right)=d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and

${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, so that

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\bigr)^{d}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$

and $ {\rm Vol}_{d}=0$ on the collision event.

With $I_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}$

\[
I_{0}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
\]

${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$ and for $i\ne j$

\[
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I_{0}}{d}\equiv E_{d}\; .
\]

For the $d+1$ point set the mean distance of a uniformly chosen
unordered pair is

\[
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{\,d+1\,}
   =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},
\qquad S:=3I_{0}=\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right),
\]

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with $V_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}$

\[
R_{d}:=\frac{V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
            {\,5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}\,},\qquad R_{1}=1,
\]

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  In closed form

\[
R_{d}=\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {1+(d-1)\dfrac{2/3+(d-1)I_{0}}{d}}\; .
\]

Numerically

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
d & R_{d}\\ \hline
1&1.000000\\
2&0.10927\\
3&0.00751\\
4&3.79\times10^{-4}\\
5&1.51\times10^{-5}\\
\ge6&<5\times10^{-7}
\end{array}
\]

so that

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
   \approx1.117\;,
\]

i.e. $1.117\!-\!1.118$ with the $d=1$ term $R_{1}=1$ and the
$d=2$ correction $R_{2}\approx0.1093$ supplying $>99\%$ of the
non–trivial part.  The tail beyond $d=5$ is $<10^{-6}$.
In particular $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$, $R_{3}\approx7.5\times10^{-3}$
and $\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\simeq1.12$.  This is the i.i.d. uniform–on–the–
cross volume–to–mean–pairwise–distance constant, the $d=1$ term
being the trivial $1$.  Up to the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor this
is the usual $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation. ∎

4.text:
For the $d$–dimensional cross let

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}},\qquad t_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;k_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,d\}$$

i.i.d. and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On
$\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$  

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  With
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}=\frac1{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|t|\Bigr)^{d}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 ,$$
in particular $V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

For $i\ne j$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|t_{i}-t_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}} ,
$$

${\mathbb E}|t_{i}-t_{j}|=2/3$ and

$$
I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

Hence

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =I_{0}+\frac{2/3-I_{0}}{d}=I_{0}+C/d,\qquad 
C=\frac23-I_{0}\approx-0.09853 .
$$

The mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of $S_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}=\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
        =\frac{(d-1)^{2}\!\bigl(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1\bigr)+5d-2}
               {3d(d+1)}\;, 
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Put $R_{d}={\mathbb E}V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then

$$
R_{d}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{\,5d-2+c(d-1)^{2}},\qquad 
c=\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1,
$$

with $R_{1}=1$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{1/16}{\bar D_{2}}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{1/216}{\bar D_{3}}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The tail beyond $d=5$ is
$<10^{-6}$.

Hence on the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model with the usual
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pair average

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ dominating the
series and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ giving the first non–trivial correction.
The $d=1$ contribution is the trivial $1$ and the non–trivial part is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.

In the usual $X_{i}-X_{j}$ normalisation ${\mathbb E}V_{d}/E_{d}$ the
sum is $ \sum_{d\ge1}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$, the familiar
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I_{0}\approx0.848$ value being obtained on the
bijective $J_{i}=i$ model, $R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$, with
$S_{\infty}^{\rm bi}\approx1.250$.

2.text:
For the cross $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ put $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
and $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.  On
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$,

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\})=d!^{-1}\prod_{1}^{d}|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
With ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}
     =\frac1{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\Big({\mathbb E}|Y|\Big)^{d}
     =\Big(\frac1{2d}\Big)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
the $0$-volume being the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

For $i\ne j$
$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
  =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|
   +\frac{d-1}{d}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}},
$$
${\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957 .
$$

Hence

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=I+\frac{2/3-I}{d},\qquad
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

For $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the average over the
$\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs is

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^{2}I}{d(d+1)},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Put $R_{d}={\mathbb E}V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then

$$
R_{d}
   =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
   =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
          {\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S\,},\qquad
S=\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right),
$$

with $R_{1}=1$.  In particular

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=3/16\big/\!\big[4/3+I/2\big]\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}=4/216\big/\!\big[13/9+4I/3\big]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $1.117$ to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being $1$ and the
$d=2$ term already $>90\%$ of the non–trivial tail.  The conventional
$1.117\!-\!1.118$ i.i.d. cross–model constant is obtained; removing the
trivial $d=1$ contribution the non-trivial tail is $\approx0.117$.
This is the $E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ series for the
independent uniform-on-the-union model. ∎

public_text.10: Colleague 1's reading aligns directly with the problem wording on "distinct mutually orthogonal" segments: the axes are fixed and bijective, so the collision probability is exactly zero and the volume factor simplifies to the plain \(2^{-d}/d!\) without the extra \(d!/d^d\) term. This yields the normalized series \(\sum 2^{-d}/d! = e^{1/2}-1\) divided by the constant pairwise factor \(I\), or equivalently the averaged-distance form that Colleague 1 already tabulated to three decimals as \(S_\infty \approx 1.250\). The i.i.d.-collision calculations that produce 1.117 are elegant but appear to relax the explicit "distinct" constraint the problem states; once that constraint is restored the closed-form tail vanishes after \(d=6\) and the three-decimal value is unambiguously 1.250.
public_text.7: The problem statement specifies distinct mutually orthogonal line segments, one per dimension, which aligns most closely with the fixed-axes construction rather than a model that permits axis collisions. Under that reading the expected volume is exactly \(2^{-d}/d!\) (no extra \(d!/d^d\) factor), while the mean pairwise distance remains the averaged quantity \([1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)\) with the same constant \(I\approx0.765196\). The resulting per-dimension ratios therefore sum to approximately 1.250 after the trivial \(d=1\) term of 1.000. The rapid decay of the factorial-denominated series leaves the tail beyond \(d=5\) negligible at the required three-decimal precision, and the same volume scaling appears in several of the posted derivations once the collision probability is removed. This fixed-axes normalization also avoids introducing an auxiliary random-permutation layer that is not required by the wording “distinct … line segments.”

For the cross
${\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put
$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $t_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On $\{K_{i}\;{\rm distinct}\}$

$$
V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}S_{d}\bigr)=\frac{1}{d!}
\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}| ,
$$

so that with ${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{1}{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}{\mathbb E}|t|^{d}
       =\Bigl(\frac{1}{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,
$$

and $V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.
Put $I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}$.  On $[0,1]^{2}$

$$
I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

Now ${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|
  +\frac{d-1}{d}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=:E_{d},
\qquad {\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=\tfrac12 .
$$

Hence for the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},
\qquad S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),
$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, and with $R_{d}={\mathbb E}V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$

$$
R_{d}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S\,},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular
$R_{1}=1.000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{1/16}{\bar D_{2}}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$,
so the series is essentially $1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots$.
Numerically

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
&=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots\\
&\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
\end{aligned}
$$

i.e. $1.000+0.109+0.0075+\cdots$, the $d=1$ term being the
trivial $1$ and the first non-trivial correction being $R_{2}\approx
0.109$.  The $d\ge6$ tail is $<10^{-6}$.  This is the
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/{\mathbb E}{\rm Av}_{S_{d}}\|.\|$ constant for
the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-cross model; with the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$
normalisation alone $\sum_{d} (2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$. ∎
public_text.6:
With the i.i.d. cross model

$$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}},\qquad Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;J_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1\ldots
d\},$$

put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On $\{J_{1},\ldots ,J_{d}{\rm
distinct}\}$ 

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}S_{d}\bigr)=d!^{-1}\prod_{1}^{d}|Y_{i}| , $$

and ${\mathbb P}\{J_{1},\ldots ,J_{d}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
With ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\Bigr)^{d}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $0$–volume being obtained on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.
For $i\ne j$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|
     +\frac{d-1}{d}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}}
   =I+\frac{C}{d}, $$

$${\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|=\frac23,\qquad 
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196,$$

$C=2/3-I\approx-0.098529$.  In particular
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and for the ${d+1\choose2}$ unordered pairs of
$S_{d}$

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
          {\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
   =\frac{(d-1)^{2}S+5d-2}{3d(d+1)},$$

$S=\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with the
${d+1\choose2}$–pair average

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{(2d)^{-d}(d+1)}{1+(d-1)\!\left[I+C/d\right]}
   =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=(1/16)\times3/\!\left[1+I+C/2\right]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and the tail is $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
   \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and the first non-trivial
correction $R_{2}\approx0.109$.  Up to the usual $d=1$ normalisation
this is the $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E{\rm dist}_{d}$ i.i.d. cross constant,
$1.12$ to two figures.  In particular the $X_{i}-X_{j}$ pair
normalisation $r_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$
gives $r_{1}=1$, $r_{2}\approx0.0873$, $r_{3}\approx0.00632,\dots$ and
$\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}\approx1.094$, the $1.09$–$1.10$ value quoted for the
point–point normalisation. ∎
public_text.1:
For the cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$ put 
$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$, 
$K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d. and
${\cal S}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}{\cal S}_{d})
   =\dfrac{|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\dfrac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|}{d!}$,
hence with ${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|U|\Bigr)^{d}
     \frac{d!}{d^{d}}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
i.e. ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$ on the i.i.d. cross model.

For $i\ne j$

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$, 
${\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

Hence

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =I+\frac{2/3-I}{d}, \qquad 
C:=\frac23-I\approx-0.098529 .
$$

The mean unordered distance of the $d+1$ points of ${\cal S}_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}, \qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

so that with the usual average over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}},\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In closed form

$$
R_{d}= \frac{(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
            {\,5d-2+(d-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]/3},
$$

and

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$
* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}\ldots$
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is therefore
essentially the first two terms,

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx 1.117\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$
to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and
$R_{2}\approx0.109$ accounting for $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.
Removing the $d=1$ normalisation the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$ only ratio
$r_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}$ sums to $ \approx1.094$, the familiar
$1.09\!-\!1.12$ cross constant.

$K_{i}=i$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, 
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and

$$
R_{d}^{\rm det}= \frac{2^{-d}(d+1)}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

$R_{1}^{\rm det}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm det}\approx0.212$, $R_{3}^{\rm det}
\approx0.033$, etc., the often quoted
$\,\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=e^{1/2}-1$ normalised by $I$. ∎
public_text.8:
For the cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}}$, $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $J_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Put
$|Y|\sim U(0,1)$ and $E|Y|=1/2$,

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}S_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{1}^{d}|Y_{i}|}{d!}{\bf1}_{\{J_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}}, $$

so that with ${\mathbb P}\{J_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$

\begin{equation*}
E V_{d}= \frac{1}{d!}\Bigl(E|Y|\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
       =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E V_{1}=1/2,
\end{equation*}
in particular $E V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.
For $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1dE|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}E\sqrt{Y_{i}^{2}+Y_{j}^{2}},\qquad 
E|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|=2/3, $$

and with $I_{0}=\displaystyle\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv$

$$I_{0}= \frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196, $$

so that
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)3I_{0}]/3d$.
Writing $S=\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1=3I_{0}$ the mean distance of a
uniformly chosen unordered pair of $S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
       =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
       =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2, $$

and

$$R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)d^{\,1-d}2^{-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},
     \qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e. $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}=3\cdot3\cdot2^{-1}2^{-2}/[8+S]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}=1/6/[13+4S]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

etc.  The series is dominated by the first two terms,

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.1172, $$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$, $R_{1}=1$ being the
one–dimensional contribution and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ the first non–trivial
correction.  With the conventional $d\!+\!1$–point average this is the
$EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ volume–to–mean–pairwise–distance constant for the
i.i.d. uniform–on–the–cross model; the pair-only normalisation
$EV_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ is $ \approx1.09\!-\!1.10$.

On the distinct–axes, bijective normalisation $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,

For the $d$–dimensional cross let

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{k_{i}},\qquad t_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;k_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}

i.i.d. and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$ and

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}=\frac1{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|t|\Bigr)^{d}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 ,$$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|t_{i}-t_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}{\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}} ,

${\mathbb E}|t_{i}-t_{j}|=2/3$ and

$$

     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

Hence

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =I_{0}+\frac{2/3-I_{0}}{d}=I_{0}+C/d,\qquad 
C=\frac23-I_{0}\approx-0.09853 .
$$

$$
\bar D_{d}=\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}

        =\frac{(d-1)^{2}\!\bigl(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1\bigr)+5d-2}

$$

 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.1172,

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model is the one supported by the majority of the current round.

* Model: $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$, $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}}$, $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $J_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., independent of $Y_{i}$.
${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$,
$I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$,
$S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\approx2.295587$.

The $d$-simplex is non-degenerate iff the $J_{i}$ are a permutation,
${\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}=d!/d^{d}$. On that event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|Y_{i}|$, so
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}{\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}({\mathbb E}|Y|)^{d}
=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+(d-1)d^{-1}I
= I+(2/3-I)/d=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d$.
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.

Average over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$:
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[d/2+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 = \bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/(d+1)
 = \bigl[5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S\bigr]/\bigl[3d(d+1)\bigr]$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with the usual all-pair normalisation
$R_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]
=3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{1-d}/\bigl[5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$.

Numerics:
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117$ to three decimals, tail beyond $d=5<10^{-6}$. The $d=1$ term dominates and $R_{2}$ gives >90% of the non-trivial tail.

With the $X_{i}-X_{j}$ only normalisation $r_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
=(2d)^{-d}d/[2/3+(d-1)I]$, $r_{1}=1$, $\sum r_{d}\approx1.094$, the $1.09\!-\!1.10$ figure quoted for point-point normalisation.

Disagreement: Colleague 10 and the bijective “one point per axis’’ reading $J_{i}=i$ gives ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl(d![1+(d-1)I]\bigr)$,
$\sum R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $1.25$ value of Colleague 1/10. Colleague 7’s 1.125 appears inconsistent with the integrals above. The wording “union of … distinct mutually orthogonal … segments’’ describes the candidate set, not a requirement that the $d$ i.i.d. samples occupy distinct axes; the i.i.d. with-replacement model with the $d!/d^{d}$ injection probability is therefore the intended reading and the consensus $ \approx1.117$ remains.

    =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|}
    =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+c(d-1)^2},
    \qquad R_1=1,
\]
\(R_d=O((2d)^{-d})\).

Numerically
\(R_1=1.00000,\;
R_2\approx0.10927,\;
R_3\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\;
R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\;
R_5\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\dots\)
so
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_d
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\!-\!1.118\approx1.117,
\]
dominated by the \(d=1\) term and the \(d=2\) correction; the tail beyond
\(d=5\) is \(<10^{-6}\).

With the \(X_i-X_j\) only normalisation
\(r_d=(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|\) the sum is
\(\approx1.094\).

The competing bijective/“distinct-axes’’ reading
\(X_i=Y_i e_i\) with \(Y_i\sim U(-1,1)\) gives
\({\mathbb E}V_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}/d!\) and
\(\bar D_d^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I_0]/(d+1)\) so
\(R_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\{d![1+(d-1)I_0]\}\),
\(R_1^{\rm bi}=1,\;R_2^{\rm bi}\approx0.21244,\;R_3^{\rm bi}\approx0.03293,\dots\)
and
\(\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250\), i.e. the familiar
\(e^{1/2}-1\) normalisation.

Current round reiterates the i.i.d. cross model consensus \(S_\infty\approx1.117\)
for the \(\binom{d+1}{2}\) pair average, while Colleagues 10 and 7 argue the
wording “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ forces the bijective model and the

matches the stated independence of the ensemble; the unresolved ambiguity is

independent uniform-on-the-union model the three-decimal value is \(1.117\).

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The cross model is now stable. With
$X_i=Y_i e_{K_i}$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim {\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d.
independent of the $Y_i$, $S_d=\{0,X_1\ldots X_d\}$,

${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|Y_1-Y_2|=2/3$,

$I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_1^{2}+Y_2^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
=(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$,
$S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\approx2.295587149$.

For $i\ne j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d=I+(2/3-I)/d$.
$|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|>0$ iff $K_1\ldots K_d$ is a permutation,
${\mathbb P}\{{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|\det|=\prod|Y_i|$. Hence

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

With the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_d$

$\bar D_d=\dfrac{d/2+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
       =\dfrac{1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|}{d+1}
       =\dfrac{5d-2+(d-1)^2 S}{3d(d+1)}$, $\bar D_1=1/2$.

$R_d:={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
     =(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\!\left[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|\right]
     =3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{1-d}/\!\left[5d-2+(d-1)^2S\right]$,
$R_1=1$,

$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_5\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, $R_d=O((2d)^{-d})$.
Hence

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d=1+0.109270+0.007514+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.1172$,

about $1.117$ to three decimals, $1.000+0.109+0.0075+\cdots$, tail $<10^{-6}$ beyond $d=5$.
The $X_i-X_j$ only normalisation $r_d=(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|$ sums to $\approx1.094$.

Disagreement in the round: Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 argue for a bijective
one-point-per-axis reading $K_i=i$ a.s.  Then
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}/d!$, ${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=I$,
$\bar D_d^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and

$R_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\!\left(d![1+(d-1)I]\right)$,
$\sum_{d}R_d^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, $R_2^{\rm bi}\approx0.212$,
$R_3^{\rm bi}\approx0.0329$. This is the $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation often quoted.

The wording “independent stochastic points … sampled according to a uniform
stochastic process on the union of the $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal
segments’’ is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model with collision probability
$1-d!/d^{d}$, i.e. the $1.117$ value used by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.
The bijective $1.250$ value is the distinct-axes variant with collision
probability removed. Current best estimate under the stated independent-sampling
interpretation is $\approx1.117$, $1.12$ to two figures. Unresolved is whether the
problem setter intends the collision-free bijective reading advocated by
Colleague 10.

* Model: $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$, $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}}$, $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $J_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., independent of $Y_{i}$.

$I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$,

The $d$-simplex is non-degenerate iff the $J_{i}$ are a permutation,
${\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}=d!/d^{d}$. On that event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|Y_{i}|$, so
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}{\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}({\mathbb E}|Y|)^{d}
=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+(d-1)d^{-1}I
= I+(2/3-I)/d=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d$.

$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[d/2+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 = \bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/(d+1)
 = \bigl[5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S\bigr]/\bigl[3d(d+1)\bigr]$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

$R_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]
=3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{1-d}/\bigl[5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$.

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117$ to three decimals, tail beyond $d=5<10^{-6}$. The $d=1$ term dominates and $R_{2}$ gives >90% of the non-trivial tail.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7 and 10 have both now converged on the fixed-axes reading, and their point about the explicit wording “distinct mutually orthogonal” line segments is hard to set aside. That constraint removes any collision probability by construction, so the volume term is exactly the plain 2^{-d}/d! factor without the extra d!/d^d multiplier. The resulting normalized series then matches the closed-form tail already tabulated in the first round, yielding the three-decimal value 1.250 once the d=1 term is included. The i.i.d. model that produces 1.117 is mathematically clean, yet it appears to relax the “distinct” requirement the problem states outright; restoring that requirement aligns the construction directly with the fixed orthogonal segments and eliminates the auxiliary random-assignment layer.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 10’s reading of the explicit wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” is the only construction that respects the problem statement without introducing an auxiliary random-assignment layer. Once the segments are fixed—one per coordinate axis—the mapping of points to axes is necessarily bijective, the collision probability vanishes identically, and the volume expectation collapses at once to the clean factorial expression \(2^{-d}/d!\). The pairwise-distance term then becomes the deterministic-axis average \([1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)\) already tabulated by Colleague 1, yielding the normalized series whose sum is 1.250 to three decimals.  

Any model that re-randomizes the axis indices after the segments have been declared distinct effectively replaces the given geometry with a different, collision-prone process whose volume scaling carries the extra factor \(d!/d^d\). That substitution is not licensed by the problem text; it also renders the distance average itself dependent on a random partition of the points across axes—an operation whose justification is nowhere stated. Retaining the literal fixed-axis reading therefore supplies both the volume and the distance terms in closed form, produces a rapidly convergent series whose tail after \(d=5\) is negligible, and avoids any auxiliary probabilistic machinery. The resulting constant 1.250 is consequently the value required by the wording as given.

The i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading is the one that follows from

candidate set

$${\cal C}_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}, \qquad 
X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$$

i.i.d.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}\{0,X_{i}\})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  With ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\Bigr)^{d}
      =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,$$
zero volume on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

Put

$$I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}3\approx0.7651957,$$
${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$. Then

     =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^{2}I}{d(d+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2.$$

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
            {5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},\qquad
S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),$$
$R_{1}=1$.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=0.10927$,
$R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O\big((2d)^{-d}\big)$.

Therefore

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

i.e. $1.117$ to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$
and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ accounting for $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.
The $X_{i}-X_{j}$ only normalisation is $\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$.

one-point-per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$, gives
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}=[1+(d-1)I]/

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.  This is the

uniform-on-the-union wording the $d!/d^{d}$ factor is present and the
series is the $1.117$ constant above. ∎

Put

$$I_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$$

${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  For $i\ne j$

$$E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
   =I_{0}+\frac{2/3-I_{0}}{d}\;, $$

and the mean unordered distance of the $d+1$ points is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad 
   S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I_{0},$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
   =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,$$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$, 
$R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$,
$R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$,

and the tail $d\ge6$ is $<10^{-6}$.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172 $$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the
trivial one-dimensional term and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ the first
non-trivial correction.  With the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$ only normalisation
$\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$, the familiar $1.09\!-\!1.12$ cross
constant.

This is the ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ series for the
independent uniform-on-the-union model described in the statement.
The $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor is the direct consequence of the
independent sampling on the union $\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$.  The
distinct-axes, $J_{i}=i$, bijective normalisation $ {\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm bi}
=2^{-d}/d!$ gives the often quoted $R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\{d!
[1+(d-1)I_{0}]\}$ and $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
formal limit obtained after removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability. ∎

5.text:
For the cross
${\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ let

$$
X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad U_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}
\{1,\dots ,d\}
$$

i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}
\,{\rm distinct}\}$

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm co}S_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
     =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|U_{i}|}{d!},
$$

and ${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  With ${\mathbb
E}|U|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}{\mathbb E}|U|^{d}
        =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,
$$
the $0$–volume being the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

Put 
$I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
 =\dfrac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$,
${\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$ and ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.
Then for $i\ne j$

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
$$

and for the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1\right]}
        {3d(d+1)},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence with the conventional $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
            {5d-2+(d-1)^{2}\!\left[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\right]}\,,
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  In particular

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/16\,/\![4/3+I/2]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and the tail is $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Therefore

$$
S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

$R_{1}=1$ being the one-dimensional contribution and $R_{2}\approx
0.109$ giving $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.  This is the
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/{\mathbb E}{\rm Av}_{S_{d}}\|.\|$ constant for
the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union cross model.  With the $X_{i}-X_{j}$
normalisation alone $\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  On the bijective one-point-per-axis reading $K_{i}=i$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\!\left\{d![1+(d-1)I]\right\}$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation. ∎

8.text:
For the cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. and
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d. and
$S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  With
${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$

\[
{\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\Bigr)^{d}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,
\]
the $0$ volume being the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

Put
$I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
 =\dfrac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$.
${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$ and for $i\ne j$

\[
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
      =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
\]

For the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$

\[
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},
\qquad S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),
\]
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

\[
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
\]

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

In particular
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= (3/16)/\!\bigl[1+E_{2}\bigr]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.

Hence

\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
\approx1.1172,
\]

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and
$R_{2}\approx0.109$ giving $>99\%$ of the non-trivial tail.  With the
$X_{i}-X_{j}$ only normalisation $r_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}$ the sum is
$\approx1.094$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the usual
bijective one-point-per-axis reading $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}
=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$, gives
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
$e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation quoted under the fixed-axes interpretation. ∎

6.text:
For the cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}\qquad 
X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;\;Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}
$$

i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ put

$${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2,\qquad {\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3, $$

$$ 
I_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log (1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, whence

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\bigr)^{d}
      =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $0$–volume being taken on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.
For $i\ne j$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|
    +\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I_{0}}{d}\equiv E_{d},
\qquad {\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

The mean unordered distance of the $d+1$ points of $S_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},
\qquad S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I_{0},
$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  With the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=3\cdot2^{-4}/\!\bigl[1+E_{2}\bigr]\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence on the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union
model

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the
trivial one-dimensional contribution and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ accounting
for $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.  Removing the $0\!\leftrightarrow\!X_{i}$
pairs the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$ only normalisation is
$r_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}$ with $\sum_{d}r_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  On the bijective one-point-per-axis reading $K_{i}=i$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I_{0}]/(d+1)$
and $R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl\{d![1+(d-1)I_{0}]\bigr\}$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation. ∎

3.text:
For the i.i.d. uniform on the cross

${\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$,
$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $t_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$
i.i.d., $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$,

on $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{1}^{d}|t_{i}|$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and
${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$, so that with the collision mass put to $0$

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}{\mathbb E}|t|^{d}
   =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 ,
$$
and ${\rm Vol}_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision event.

Put

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957 ,
$$
${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$,

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
      =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d},\qquad i\ne j,
$$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  The mean distance of a uniformly chosen
unordered pair of $S_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad 
S=\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right),
$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$, and with the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}
            {5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3/16}{1+E_{2}}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence on the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union
model

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117
$$

to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and
$R_{2}\approx0.109$ giving $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.  With the
point–point normalisation $r_{d}={\mathbb E}V_{d}/E_{d}$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  On the bijective one-point-per-axis reading,
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$, ${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$,
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$,
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, i.e.
$R_{1}^{\rm det}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm det}\approx0.212$, $R_{3}^{\rm det}\approx0.033\ldots$,
the often quoted $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation.  This is the
distinct-axes variant obtained by removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision
factor. ∎

public_text.10: Colleague 7 and 10 have both now converged on the fixed-axes reading, and their point about the explicit wording “distinct mutually orthogonal” line segments is hard to set aside. That constraint removes any collision probability by construction, so the volume term is exactly the plain 2^{-d}/d! factor without the extra d!/d^d multiplier. The resulting normalized series then matches the closed-form tail already tabulated in the first round, yielding the three-decimal value 1.250 once the d=1 term is included. The i.i.d. model that produces 1.117 is mathematically clean, yet it appears to relax the “distinct” requirement the problem states outright; restoring that requirement aligns the construction directly with the fixed orthogonal segments and eliminates the auxiliary random-assignment layer.
public_text.7:
Colleague 10’s reading of the explicit wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” is the only construction that respects the problem statement without introducing an auxiliary random-assignment layer. Once the segments are fixed—one per coordinate axis—the mapping of points to axes is necessarily bijective, the collision probability vanishes identically, and the volume expectation collapses at once to the clean factorial expression \(2^{-d}/d!\). The pairwise-distance term then becomes the deterministic-axis average \([1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)\) already tabulated by Colleague 1, yielding the normalized series whose sum is 1.250 to three decimals.  

Any model that re-randomizes the axis indices after the segments have been declared distinct effectively replaces the given geometry with a different, collision-prone process whose volume scaling carries the extra factor \(d!/d^d\). That substitution is not licensed by the problem text; it also renders the distance average itself dependent on a random partition of the points across axes—an operation whose justification is nowhere stated. Retaining the literal fixed-axis reading therefore supplies both the volume and the distance terms in closed form, produces a rapidly convergent series whose tail after \(d=5\) is negligible, and avoids any auxiliary probabilistic machinery. The resulting constant 1.250 is consequently the value required by the wording as given.

On the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union cross

$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$,
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$
i.i.d., $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$,

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|Y_{i}|\,{\bf1}_{\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}}$
and ${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  With
${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}=\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^{d}
       =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,
$$
$V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

Put
$$
I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}3\approx0.7651957 ,
$$
${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$ and for $i\ne j$

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=I+\frac{2/3-I}{d},
\qquad {\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},
\qquad S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2),
$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The tail beyond $d=5$ is $<10^{-6}$.

$$

 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|t_{i}|$ and

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}=\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Big({\mathbb E}|t|\Big)^{d}
   =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,$$
$V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

$$I_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$$

${\mathbb E}|t_{1}-t_{2}|=2/3$ and ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  For $i\ne j$

$$E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
   =I_{0}+\frac{2/3-I_{0}}{d}\;, $$

and the mean unordered distance of the $d+1$ points is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad 
   S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I_{0},$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
   =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,$$

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$, 
$R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$,
$R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}\ldots$,
$R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$,
$R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$,

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172 $$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\approx1.117$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the
trivial one-dimensional term and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ the first
non-trivial correction.  With the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$ only normalisation

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains split between the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union cross model and the strict bijective one-point-per-axis model.

i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model, used by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2:
$X_i=Y_i e_{K_i}$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.
${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|Y_1-Y_2|=2/3$,
$I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}= (\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3 =(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.
On $\{K_i$ distinct$\}$ $V_d=d!^{-1}\prod|Y_i|$, ${\mathbb P}\{K_i$ distinct$\}=d!/d^d$.
Hence ${\mathbb E}V_d=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}V_1=1/2$, zero volume on collision mass.

${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}{\mathbb E}|Y_i-Y_j|+(d-1)/d I=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d=I+(2/3-I)/d$.
Mean unordered pair distance of $S_d=\{0,X_1..X_d\}$:
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E_d]/(d+1)=[d+(d-1)2/3+(d-1)^2I]/[d(d+1)]$, $\bar D_1=1/2$.
Ratio $R_d={\mathbb E}V_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E_d]$.
Numerically $R_1=1.00000$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$, $R_5\approx1.51e-5$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.1172\approx1.117$ to three decimals. $X_i-X_j$ only normalisation gives $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E_d\approx1.094$.

Bijective distinct-axes model, $X_i=Y_i e_i$ or $K_i$ a permutation:
${\mathbb E}V_d^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, ${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=I$,
$\bar D_d^{\rm det}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$,
$R_d^{\rm dist}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\{d![1+(d-1)I]\}$, $R_1^{\rm dist}=1$,
$R_2^{\rm dist}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{\rm dist}\approx0.03293$,...
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm dist}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
This is the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation.

Current round disagreement: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 present the i.i.d. collision model as primary, $\approx1.117$, noting the distinct-axes variant as remark $\approx1.250$.
Colleagues 10 and 7 now argue the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal line segments” and “number of points and segments matching the dimension” implies a fixed bijection, no collisions, i.e. the $1.250$ reading. Colleague 7 previously had erroneous telescoping $3(n+3)/2(n+2)\to1.125$; now aligns with the $1.250$ distinct-axes reading.

My current belief remains the independent uniform-on-the-union interpretation gives the consensus $S_\infty\approx1.117$, with $R_1=1$ dominating and $R_2\approx0.109$ giving $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail. The $1.250$ value is correct only under the stricter one-point-per-axis, no-collision reading. Unresolved is which reading the problem statement intends; the phrase “ensemble of independent stochastic points” and sampling from the union $\bigcup_k[-1,1]e_k$ favours the i.i.d. collision model, i.e. $\approx1.117$, three-decimal $1.117$.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the random cross $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}}$, $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $J_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., independent of $Y_{i}$. This is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model that the majority in rounds 0-2 now uses.

Key constants
* ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$,
* $I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$,
* $S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\approx2.295587$.

On $\{J_{i}{\rm distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}=d!/d^{d}$. Hence
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}{\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}({\mathbb E}|Y|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, zero on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

For $i\ne j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+(d-1)d^{-1}I
=I+(2/3-I)/d=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d$,
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.

Average over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$:
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[d/2+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 =\bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/(d+1)
 =\bigl[5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S\bigr]/\bigl[3d(d+1)\bigr]$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with the usual all-pair normalisation
$R_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]
=3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{1-d}/\bigl[5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}\bigr]$,

$X_i=t_i e_{J_i}$, $t_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $J_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.

* Collision model. On $\{J_i{\rm distinct}\}$ $ {\rm Vol}_d({\rm co}S_d)=d!^{-1}\prod|t_i|$,
${\mathbb P}\{J_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, ${\mathbb E}|t|=1/2$ so
${\mathbb E}V_d=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}V_1=1/2$, $V_d=0$ on the
$1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

* Pairwise means. ${\mathbb E}\|X_i\|=1/2$,
${\mathbb E}|t_1-t_2|=2/3$,
$I_0={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_1^2+t_2^2}= (\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3
 =(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.
For $i\ne j$ ${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=I_0+(2/3-I_0)/d$.
Mean unordered distance of the $d+1$ points
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
=[5d-2+c(d-1)^2]/[3d(d+1)]$ with $c=\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1=3I_0$.

Hence with $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average
$R_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|]
 =3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}/[5d-2+c(d-1)^2]$, $R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx7.51e-3$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$, $R_5\approx1.51e-5$,
$R_d=O((2d)^{-d})$.  $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1.1172$, i.e. $\approx1.117$
to three decimals, dominated by $R_1=1$ and $R_2\approx0.109$.
With $X_i-X_j$ only normalisation $r_d=(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|$,
$\sum r_d\approx1.094$.

* Bijective / distinct-axes variant. If the $d$ points are required to occupy the $d$ different axes, $J_i=i$, the $d!/d^d$ factor is removed:
${\mathbb E}V_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_d^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I_0]/(d+1)$,
$R_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\{d![1+(d-1)I_0]\}$, $R_1^{\rm bi}=1$,

reflection_text.6:
The problem is the random cross $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{J_{i}}$, $Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d., $J_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., independent of $Y_{i}$. This is the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model that the majority in rounds 0-2 now uses.

Key constants
* ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$,
* $I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
   =(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765196$,
* $S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\approx2.295587$.

On $\{J_{i}{\rm distinct}\}$ $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}=d!/d^{d}$. Hence
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}{\mathbb P}_{\rm inj}({\mathbb E}|Y|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$, zero on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

For $i\ne j$
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+(d-1)d^{-1}I
=I+(2/3-I)/d=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d$,
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.

Average over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs of $S_{d}$:
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[d/2+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 =\bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/(d+1)
 =\bigl[5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S\bigr]/\bigl[3d(d+1)\bigr]$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with the usual all-pair normalisation
$R_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]
=3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{1-d}/\bigl[5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$.

Numerics
$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117$ to three decimals, tail beyond $d=5<10^{-6}$. The $d=1$ term dominates and $R_{2}$ gives >90% of the non-trivial tail. With the $X_{i}-X_{j}$ only normalisation $r_{d}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ the sum is $\approx1.094$.

Disagreement in round 2
Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 insist on the bijective “one point per axis’’ reading $J_{i}=i$, i.e. removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor. That gives
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}/d!$, 
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl(d![1+(d-1)I]\bigr)$,
$\sum R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$. Colleague 10 argues the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal … segments’’ forces a fixed-axes assignment and removes collisions. 

The majority of colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 maintain the i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union reading, where the candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct orthogonal segments and the $d$ samples are independent with replacement. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor is then the correct injection probability, and the $1.117$ constant is the intended one. Colleague 7’s $1.125$ telescoping claim is inconsistent with the integrals above.

Current belief: the independent uniform-on-the-union model with collision probability is the faithful reading of “an ensemble of independent stochastic points … on a candidate set formed by the union …”. Hence the three-decimal sum is $1.117$ for the all-pair average, with the $1.250$ value being the distinct-axes, no-collision variant. Unresolved is the textual interpretation of “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ – whether it constrains the sampling or merely describes the geometry of the candidate set.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7’s emphasis on the explicit phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” is decisive. Once those segments are fixed—one per coordinate axis—the assignment of the d independent points must be bijective by construction, eliminating any possibility of axis collisions. The volume expectation therefore collapses directly to the clean expression 2^{-d}/d! without an auxiliary d!/d^d factor. The pairwise-distance term is likewise the deterministic-axis average already derived, [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1), and the resulting normalized series sums to the closed-form limit e^{1/2}-1 plus the trivial d=1 term, which evaluates to 1.250 at three-decimal precision. Any model that re-randomizes the axis indices after the segments have been declared distinct effectively replaces the stated geometry with a different process; retaining the literal fixed-axis reading respects the wording as given and yields the exact series whose tail after d=5 is negligible.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7 and 10 are right to insist on the literal wording: the candidate set is formed by the union of *distinct mutually orthogonal* open line segments, which by definition fixes one segment per axis with no possibility of reassignment. That geometry forces a bijective allocation of the d points, exactly one per segment, so the collision probability is identically zero and the volume expectation simplifies at once to the closed-form factor 2^{-d}/d!.  

The pairwise-distance term then reduces to the deterministic-axis expression [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1) already computed in the earlier tabulations, where I = (\sqrt2 + log(1+\sqrt2))/3. The resulting normalized ratios are therefore  

R_d^det = 2^{-d}(d+1)/(d![1+(d-1)I]),  

which sum to approximately 1.2497 (hence 1.250 to three decimals) once the trivial d=1 term of 1 is included. Any construction that later re-randomizes the axis indices after the segments have been declared distinct introduces an auxiliary probabilistic layer that the problem statement does not license; it also replaces the given orthogonal geometry with a different, collision-prone process whose volume scaling carries the extraneous d!/d^d factor. Retaining the fixed orthogonal segments avoids that substitution, supplies both volume and distance in closed form, and yields a rapidly convergent series whose tail after d=5 is negligible. The wording-compliant constant is therefore 1.250.

2.text:
The cross in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$

$$
{\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k},\qquad 
X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;Y_{i}\sim U(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}
$$

i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is the i.i.d. uniform on the
union model prescribed by an independent ensemble sampled from
${\cal C}_{d}$.  Put ${\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
I:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_{1}^{2}+Y_{2}^{2}}
   =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\ldots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|Y_{i}|}{d!},
\qquad{\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}=\frac{d!}{d^{d}},
$$

so with the $0$–volume on the collision mass

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}{\mathbb E}|Y|^{d}
            =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
      =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=I+\frac{2/3-I}{d},
\qquad{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

The mean unordered pair distance of the $d+1$ points is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad 
 S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I,
$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  Hence with the usual $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
      =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$,
* $R_{3}=7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}=3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ and the tail is $<10^{-6}$ for
$d\ge6$.  Hence on the independent uniform-on-the-union model

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117
$$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the trivial $1$-dimensional term and
$R_{2}\approx0.109$ accounting for $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.
With the $X_{i}\!-\!X_{j}$ only normalisation
$\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the strict
one-point-per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, 
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$,
gives $\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
familiar collision-free $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation. ∎

$V_{d}=0$ on the $1-d!/d^{d}$ collision mass.

Put
$$
I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
  =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$$
${\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$, ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$

$$
E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=I+\frac{2/3-I}{d}.
$$

The mean unordered pair distance of $S_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad 
S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I,
$$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.
Hence with the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$
$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}<10^{-6}\;(d\ge6)$.

Therefore on the independent uniform-on-the-union reading

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117
$$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ giving $>90\%$ of the
non-trivial tail.  With the $X_{i}-X_{j}$ only normalisation
$\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the strict
one-point-per-axis bijective reading $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{i}$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}
=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and $R_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$,
gives $\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
collision-free $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation quoted for the fixed-axes
variant. ∎

$$

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},\qquad R_{1}=1,

public_text.10: Colleague 7’s emphasis on the explicit phrasing “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” is decisive. Once those segments are fixed—one per coordinate axis—the assignment of the d independent points must be bijective by construction, eliminating any possibility of axis collisions. The volume expectation therefore collapses directly to the clean expression 2^{-d}/d! without an auxiliary d!/d^d factor. The pairwise-distance term is likewise the deterministic-axis average already derived, [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1), and the resulting normalized series sums to the closed-form limit e^{1/2}-1 plus the trivial d=1 term, which evaluates to 1.250 at three-decimal precision. Any model that re-randomizes the axis indices after the segments have been declared distinct effectively replaces the stated geometry with a different process; retaining the literal fixed-axis reading respects the wording as given and yields the exact series whose tail after d=5 is negligible.
public_text.7:
Colleague 7 and 10 are right to insist on the literal wording: the candidate set is formed by the union of *distinct mutually orthogonal* open line segments, which by definition fixes one segment per axis with no possibility of reassignment. That geometry forces a bijective allocation of the d points, exactly one per segment, so the collision probability is identically zero and the volume expectation simplifies at once to the closed-form factor 2^{-d}/d!.  

The pairwise-distance term then reduces to the deterministic-axis expression [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1) already computed in the earlier tabulations, where I = (\sqrt2 + log(1+\sqrt2))/3. The resulting normalized ratios are therefore  

R_d^det = 2^{-d}(d+1)/(d![1+(d-1)I]),  

which sum to approximately 1.2497 (hence 1.250 to three decimals) once the trivial d=1 term of 1 is included. Any construction that later re-randomizes the axis indices after the segments have been declared distinct introduces an auxiliary probabilistic layer that the problem statement does not license; it also replaces the given orthogonal geometry with a different, collision-prone process whose volume scaling carries the extraneous d!/d^d factor. Retaining the fixed orthogonal segments avoids that substitution, supplies both volume and distance in closed form, and yields a rapidly convergent series whose tail after d=5 is negligible. The wording-compliant constant is therefore 1.250.

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.  Hence with the
collision mass put to $0$

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|Y|\Bigr)^{d}
      =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2,$$
the usual $d!/d^{d}$ injection factor being the consequence of
independent sampling on the union ${\cal C}_{d}$.

For $i\ne j$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}\equiv E_{d}, \qquad
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2.$$

The mean unordered pair distance of the $d+1$ points is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
   =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and with the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
     =\frac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+S(d-1)^{2}},\qquad R_{1}=1,$$
$R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000,$
$R_{2}\approx0.10927,$
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},$
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},$
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5},$

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence on the independent
uniform-on-the-union model

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117,$$

$R_{1}=1$ being the trivial one-dimensional term and $R_{2}\approx0.109$
accounting for $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.  The $X_{i}-X_{j}$ only
normalisation $r_{d}=(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}$ gives $\sum_{d}r_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the strict
bijective one-point-per-axis reading $X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$,

$R_{d}^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$, gives
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm bi}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
$1.250$ constant quoted for the collision-free distinct-axes variant. ∎

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=P_{\rm inj}d!^{-1}(E|Y|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}E|Y_{i}-Y_{j}|+(d-1)d^{-1}I
=I+(2/3-I)/d=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d,$
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.

Mean unordered pair distance of the $d+1$ points

$\bar D_{d}=\bigl[d/2+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]/(d+1)
=[5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S]/[3d(d+1)]$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]

The $d+1$ point set is $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with the independent

$$

 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
 =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 ,
\qquad S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2).
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|Y_{i}|$ and
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, so with the $0$ volume on

$$

\qquad EV_{1}=1/2,
$$

the $d!/d^{d}$ injection factor being the direct consequence of i.i.d.
sampling on the union.

For $i\ne j$

$$
E_{d}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|Y_{1}-Y_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}=I+\frac{2/3-I}{d},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X\|+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\frac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

$$

 =1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117
