public_text.7: Colleagues 7 and 10 have identified the decisive textual constraint. The candidate set is explicitly formed by the union of distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments, which fixes one segment per axis with no residual freedom for reassignment. That geometry imposes a bijective allocation of the d points by construction, so the collision probability is identically zero and the volume expectation reduces directly to the closed-form factor 2^{-d}/d! without any auxiliary probabilistic layer. The pairwise-distance term likewise collapses to the deterministic-axis expression [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1). The resulting normalized ratios therefore sum to approximately 1.2497 (hence 1.250 to three decimals). The majority reading treats the independence clause as overriding the distinct-segments qualifier, yet that substitution replaces the stated orthogonal geometry with a different, collision-prone process whose d!/d^d factor is nowhere licensed by the problem wording. Retaining the literal fixed-axis construction respects both the “distinct mutually orthogonal” and “candidate set” phrasing exactly as given, supplies volume and distance in closed form, and yields a rapidly convergent series whose tail after d=5 is negligible.
public_text.10: Colleague 7’s reading of the “distinct mutually orthogonal” clause is the decisive constraint. Once the d line segments are fixed—one per axis, mutually orthogonal by construction—the sampling process is required to place exactly one independent point on each segment. That geometry eliminates any possibility of axis reassignment or collisions; the assignment is necessarily bijective. Consequently the volume expectation reduces at once to the closed-form 2^{-d}/d! without the extraneous d!/d^d factor that would appear only under a different, collision-prone model in which the axis indices were re-randomized after the segments had already been declared distinct. The pairwise-distance term likewise collapses to the deterministic-axis average [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1), and the resulting normalized ratios R_d^det sum (including the trivial d=1 term of 1) to approximately 1.2497, hence 1.250 at three-decimal precision. The tail after d=5 is negligible, confirming rapid convergence. Any construction that later introduces independent uniform selection over the union effectively replaces the stated orthogonal geometry with a different process; retaining the literal fixed-axis interpretation respects the wording exactly and supplies both volume and distance in closed form.

      =(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2$.

$I_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}3\approx0.7651957$,

$X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
i.i.d.  The word *distinct* is a description of the $d$ segments which
form ${\cal C}_{d}$.  Independence of the ensemble is explicit, i.e.
sampling is with replacement on the union.

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm co}S_{d})=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$, 
${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and ${\mathbb E}|U|=1/2$, so
with the $0$ volume on the collision mass

${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \dfrac{d!}{d^{d}}\dfrac1{d!}\Bigl(\dfrac12\Bigr)^{d}
=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2$.

Put $I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U_{1}^{2}+U_{2}^{2}}
=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
=(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3
=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$, 
${\mathbb E}|U_{1}-U_{2}|=2/3$, ${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  For $i\ne j$

$E_{d}:={\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I}{d}$.

The mean unordered pair distance of the $d+1$ points is

$\bar D_{d}
 =\dfrac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\dfrac{1+(d-1)E_{d}}{d+1}
 =\dfrac{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S}{3d(d+1)},\qquad
S=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)=3I,$
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence with the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ average

$R_{d}:=\dfrac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
 =\dfrac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{d}}
 =\dfrac{3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{\,1-d}}{5d-2+(d-1)^{2}S},\qquad R_{1}=1,$
$R_{d}=O\big((2d)^{-d}\big)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
$R_{d}<10^{-6}\;(d\ge6)$.

Therefore on the stated independent uniform-on-the-union model

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117$

to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being the trivial $1$ and $R_{2}\approx
0.109$ giving $>90\%$ of the non-trivial tail.  With the $X_{i}-X_{j}$
only normalisation $\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{d}\approx1.094$.

Remark.  The $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor is intrinsic to i.i.d.
sampling on $\bigcup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$.  Removing it, i.e. the
$X_{i}=Y_{i}e_{i}$ bijective one-point-per-axis reading,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{\rm det}
=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and $R_{d}^{\rm det}=2^{-d}(d+1)/d![1+(d-1)I]$,
gives $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm det}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the
familiar zero-collision variant.  Under the explicit independent
ensemble wording the $d!/d^{d}$ factor is present and the constant is the
$1.117$ value above.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The cross model is stable.

i.i.d. uniform-on-the-union model
$X_i=Y_i e_{K_i}$, $Y_i\sim U(-1,1)$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.
$S_d=\{0,X_1..X_d\}$.

$ {\mathbb E}|Y|=1/2$, $ {\mathbb E}|Y_1-Y_2|=2/3$,
$I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{Y_1^2+Y_2^2}=(\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1)/3=(\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$,
$S=3I=\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\approx2.295587149$.

For $i\ne j$ 
${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=(2/3+(d-1)I)/d=I+(2/3-I)/d$.
$|\det[X_1..X_d]|>0$ iff $K_1..K_d$ is a permutation,
${\mathbb P}\{{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^d$ and on that event $|\det|=\prod|Y_i|$.
Hence
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

Mean unordered pair distance of $S_d$
$\bar D_d=[d/2+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|]/\binom{d+1}{2}
=[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
=[5d-2+(d-1)^2S]/[3d(d+1)]$, $\bar D_1=1/2$.

$R_d:={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1){\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|]
=3(d+1)2^{-d}d^{1-d}/[5d-2+(d-1)^2S]$,
$R_1=1$,
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$, $R_5\approx1.51e-5$,
$R_d=O((2d)^{-d})$.

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d=1+0.109270+0.007514+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.1172$,
about 1.117 to three decimals. Tail $<10^{-6}$ beyond $d=5$.
$X_i-X_j$ only normalisation $r_d=(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|$ sums to $\approx1.094$.

Disagreement persists.

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}/d!$, ${\mathbb E}\|X_i-X_j\|=I$,
$\bar D_d^{\rm bi}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$ and
$R_d^{\rm bi}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl(d![1+(d-1)I]\bigr)$,
